name: Java Keywords and Identifiers
overview: Some Java words already have jobs. Learn which names you can use, then turn a handful of bad identifiers into names a teammate would thank you for.

sections.title: Words Java already uses
sections.content: Reserved words such as class and return cannot be names you choose. Words such as record have special meaning in certain contexts.

images.caption: Reserved keywords, contextual keywords, and literals follow different rules.

sections.title: Names the compiler accepts
sections.content: Identifiers are case-sensitive and can use Unicode. A digit cannot come first, and a single underscore is reserved. studentAge works. 2students does not.

sections.title: Names teammates can read
sections.content: Use camelCase for methods and variables, PascalCase for types, and UPPER_SNAKE_CASE for constants. Choose names that say what the value or method does.

keyPoints: Fix 2students, student-age, and int class. Use camelCase for variables, PascalCase for types, and UPPER_SNAKE_CASE for constants.

references.title: Java Language Specification (JLS) - Chapter 3: Lexical Structure

interviewQA.question: Are age and Age the same identifier?
interviewQA.answer: No. Java distinguishes uppercase and lowercase letters.

interviewQA.question: Can you declare a variable named class?
interviewQA.answer: No. class is a reserved keyword. Choose a name such as className.
